## EMST role: Natural resource and environmental programme manager (state variant, senior level; P1)

*Match:* `skos:relatedMatch`, confidence 0.4, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-wa:R13-resource-program-manager/state:523W`). *Authority position (editorial):* regulator.

**Competency targets at this level (editorial draft target levels, agent-drafted)**

- Formulate, justify and execute public budgets across appropriations cycles — senior L3
- Prepare and revise management plans for publicly held lands — senior L3
- Brief decision-makers and elected officials for authoritative decisions — senior L3
- Design developmental work experiences that preserve the formation of professional judgment — senior L3
- Elicit, document and transfer tacit and institutional knowledge before people leave — senior L3
- Design and administer cross-jurisdictional stewardship agreements — senior L3
- Administer contracts, grants and intergovernmental agreements — senior L3
- Assess the durability and reversal risk of policy choices and time actions to policy windows — senior L3
- Deliver environmental projects to budget, schedule and quality — senior L3
- Track regulatory change and translate it into operating guidance — senior L3
- Navigate legislative and governing-body processes for environmental programs — senior L3
- Evaluate and certify others' task performance against position standards — senior L3
- Apply systems thinking across ecological, institutional and technical systems — senior L3
- Apply safety practices and stop-work authority across field, facility and incident settings — senior L3
- Develop proposals and grant applications for environmental work — senior L3
- Specify, evaluate and accept AI and analytics services in procurement — senior L3
- Interpret and question environmental data products in everyday work — senior L2
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — senior L2
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — senior L2
- Record provenance and AI involvement in work products — senior L2
- Conduct job analyses and write job-related assessments for technical positions — senior L3
- Justify positions and staffing with workload and mission evidence — senior L3
- Set programme strategy and lead organizational and technological change in environmental programmes — senior L3
- Run the adaptive management cycle and evaluate programme performance — senior L3
- Supervise staff and volunteers in environmental work — senior L3
- Communicate technical environmental information in writing and speech — senior L3
- Apply merit-based, job-related practices in recruitment and team management — senior L3
- Develop and compare policy and land-use scenarios for environmental decisions — senior L3

**Main tasks at this level (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

*Critical and needed-at-entry tasks: Assessment pending (job analysis).*

- Prepare a program budget request and justification linking each funding increment to outputs and outcomes the budget office can verify
- Reconcile program obligations and expenditures against appropriations, agreements and fee accounts each month, flagging any use outside purpose or period
- Prepare a continuing-resolution and funding-lapse contingency plan, ranking program activities by legal requirement and consequence of delay
- Classify each instrument a program relies on by type and the process needed to change it, recording who can change it and how quickly
- Write a decision memo for an accountable official, stating the decision required, options, evidence, risks and a recommendation within two pages
- Brief a decision-maker orally on a pending decision under time pressure, answering questions and stating where the evidence is uncertain
- Advise an official in writing when the evidence does not support a preferred option, recording the advice given in the decision file
- Prepare a staff report for a governing body's public meeting, stating findings, options and the legal basis for each recommended action
- Track bills, ordinances and appropriations measures affecting the program, summarizing each relevant provision's effect on program operations
- Write a dated change notice explaining what a new rule, guidance or court decision changes for staff, its effective dates and the work in progress it affects
- Train staff on a significant regulatory change, testing their application of the new requirement on sample cases
- Draft a memorandum of understanding or interagency agreement that assigns shared responsibilities, resources and decision rights for a joint program
